sources.entry: BeMyEars - Live captioning tool with on-device transcription and multilingual support. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: BeMyEars
summary.one_liner: BeMyEars is a macOS app that shows system-wide live captions and on-device translated subtitles for any audio playing on the Mac.
use_cases: Reading live subtitles for videos or calls that lack captions
Captioning Zoom, Skype, Google Meet or browser audio
Translating spoken audio into your language in real time
Recording and exporting transcribed audio of online classes or meetings
summary.what_it_does: BeMyEars captures the audio played by macOS and turns it into real-time subtitles displayed system-wide, with sub-second delay according to the page. It offers on-device live translation into the user's language for 10+ supported languages, which requires macOS 15 or later. It can record the transcribed voice and export it as an m4a audio file. The page states that processing uses Apple's CoreML and Speech frameworks on the device and that audio is not uploaded. It also warns when the voice is too loud to protect hearing.
notable: On-device processing via Apple CoreML and Speech frameworks; audio not uploaded
Works with any app playing audio on macOS, not just one platform
Exports transcribed voice as m4a audio
caveats: Realtime translation requires macOS 15 or later
First use may need a language model download that can take a long time depending on network speed
Listed as Freeware in awesome-mac; the page itself does not state a price
